notes: Likely clean; no convincing token-specific fixed-target circuit identified. All evidence is checkpoint-only weight algebra, not behavioral verification. Embedding row norms have median 0.4143, p99 1.4964 and maximum 4.6606 (token 885); other large rows include 524 (3.9372), 849 (3.0554), 972 (3.0497), 451 (2.6771), and 618 (2.3002). Large rows occupy several different coordinates and favor different classes, so norm outliers alone are not evidence of a trigger. Direct virtual paths favor class 7 for 885/524/849, class 4 for 618, and class 1 for 451. After centering and unit-normalizing embedding directions, the direct-path maximum is 3.7044 versus p99 3.5411, and the linear MLP-path maximum is 0.9413 versus p99 0.8025; neither reveals an isolated dominant trigger. Head 1 OV is highly concentrated (top singular value 0.12835, 99.736% squared singular-value energy), compared with head 0 top singular value 0.00599. Including ln1 scales, head 1 mainly reads centered coordinate 2. ln1 scale at coordinate 2 is -1.8492; positional coordinate 2 is [0.5533,0.8182,0.7474,0.1103], consistent with a possible position-selection mechanism. Head 1 query-bias key preference favors token 161, whose negative coordinate-2 direction routes toward class 7. However its unit-direction preference is 0.67385 versus 0.57763 for token 977, with several other comparable tokens; its angular OV class-7 score is 0.42234 versus 0.36039 for 977. This is a candidate examined and rejected as insufficiently specific, not a verified trigger. MLP neuron detector/write analysis shows distributed class directions rather than an isolated high-gain detector; fc1 and fc2 singular spectra are broad. Classifier row norms range 2.0501 to 3.0572 without a uniquely inflated target row. Virtual products include centering and learned LayerNorm scales but omit input-dependent normalization denominators, attention softmax and GELU gating; they are not logits or attack-success estimates. No sequences, datasets, forward passes, training, or edits were used. Comparisons are within-checkpoint heuristics: no clean reference distribution or statistically calibrated detection threshold was available. Confidence is subjective; a subtle nonlinear or position-specific backdoor cannot be excluded.
